A context window is the most text a model can attend to in one call, counted in tokens. It holds the system prompt, tool definitions, the conversation so far, tool outputs and the model's reply, and anything outside it doesn't exist for the model. For agents this is a hard limit. Every tool call adds its output to the window, so a long multi-step task fills it fast. Once it's full, older content gets cut or summarised and details are lost. Quality often drops before the limit, too, as the important parts get buried among less relevant text. Cost and latency also grow with every token you send. Good agent design treats the context as a budget:
- Keep the always-loaded instructions small.
- Fetch information only when it's needed.
- Hand bulky work to subagents that return short summaries instead of raw dumps.
- Save state to files or memory so a fresh window can pick up where the last one stopped.
